page: Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g-960s is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a local 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all scoring in the top tier. Multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores landing in the average tier. Memory performance is robust, highlighted by a strong PassMark memory score in the top quarter, while large-block memory read and write bandwidths remain in the average tier. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds of 443.84 tokens per second using a small 135M parameter model, though performance drops to average levels when processing medium 7B parameter models.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation, balanced memory-to-core ratio, and local NVMe SSD storage, this server offers a reliable resource profile for workloads requiring predictable compute performance without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and fast NVMe storage makes it highly suitable for relational databases, static web serving, Redis deployments, and moderate data processing pipelines.
description: The Vultr vx1-g-16c-64g-960s is a general-purpose virtual server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a local 960 GB NVMe SSD. While multi-core benchmarks like stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores place it in the average tier, its single-core performance is highly competitive, ranking in the top tier for single-threaded compression and decompression tasks. Memory performance is strong, and the instance excels at text generation for small language models. Lacking a GPU, this server is qualitatively cost-efficient for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for database hosting, Redis operations, static web serving, and general application hosting.
